name: Medium Brown
lede: Medium Brown is a plain descriptive name for a mid-dark golden brown, and in museum paintings it is among the most common named colors we measure.

notes.cite: Eastaugh et al., Pigment Compendium, p. 418
ColorHub library (data/library.json): source xkcd only; CIEDE2000

sections.title: A middle brown
sections.body: Paterson uses the phrase in his definitions: tortoiseshell is a medium brown, and Vandyke brown is a deep brown, sometimes a medium brown [1]. In pigment science, Eastaugh's compendium notes that zinc iron oxide pigments run from light to medium brown, depending on the zinc and iron ratio [2]. So the phrase marks a tone, not a material.

sections.title: On the list
sections.body: The library finds the color only in the xkcd survey, and its nearest everyday name is [[brown]], about six and a half units away [3]. Other close names are [[tan]], [[coffee]] and [[chocolate]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Brown mid-tones are everywhere in museum paintings: 1,695 of 23,781 contain this swatch, about 7.1 per cent, more common than 89 per cent of our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1300s at 6.4 per cent of paintings, 2.0 times the expected rate [4]. Adriaen van Ostade is its most devoted painter, using it in 11 of his 39 works here, about 5 times the baseline [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so the colors are as photographed [4].
